data.name: Dasharath
data.gender_notes: Dasharath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: King Dasharatha had ten chariots. This name comes from the Sanskrit words 'daśa' meaning 'ten' and 'ratha' meaning 'chariot'. The name Dasharath carries the meaning “Ten Chariots” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dasharath usually hope their child will grow to embody ten chariots and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of strength and leadership.
data.etymology: Dasharath belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ten Chariots.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dasharath total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dasharatha is deeply embedded in Indian mythology and is an indication of power and authority. It symbolizes the idea of an ideal king or ruler, who possesses not just the command over an army, but also the wisdom and virtues to lead his people responsibly and justly. The name is often invoked in Hindu epics, particularly in association with the epic Ramayana, where Dasharatha is the father of Lord Rama.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Dasharatha can be seen as a symbol of divine kingship or rule within an individual. It represents the notion of inner rulership, or the ability to control one's thoughts, emotions and desires, thereby transforming one into an ideal 'ruler' of one's own life. Essentially, it signifies self-mastery and self-realization, reminding us that the greatest journey of all is the journey inwards, towards the discovery of the true self.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dasharath: Ten chariots or embodiment of righteousness and duty (dharma) for his subjects, symbolizing a just and virtuous ruler.

historical_references.reference: Dasharath was the king of Ayodhya mentioned in the Indian epic Ramayana. He was the father of Prince Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, and Bharata.
historical_references.context: The Ramayana is an ancient Indian epic attributed to the sage Valmiki. It tells the story of Rama, a prince of the Raghu Dynasty, and follows his journey to reclaim his wife Sita, who is abducted by the demon king Ravana.

historical_references.reference: Dasharath is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, another major Sanskrit epic of ancient India. He is described as the father of Bharata, who was the eldest of the Pandava brothers.
historical_references.context: The Mahabharata is an ancient Sanskrit epic that narrates the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes of the Kuru clan. It is traditionally believed that it was composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Dasharath is prominent in Indian mythology, specifically in the Hindu epic Ramayana, where he is the name of the king of Ayodhya who is the father of Lord Rama. In modern times, the name Dasharath is seen on various platforms. On Star Plus (India), there is a popular television show named 'Ramayan' which has been adapted from the epic and has been aired multiple times. On Netflix, there is a series named 'The Legend of Hanuman' which depicts the life of Lord Hanuman, and in one episode, Dasharath is portrayed as the king who gives the boon to Hanuman. On YouTube, there are numerous videos that retell the story of Ramayana and other Hindu epics, and Dasharath is a recurring character. The name Dasharath continues to be popular in modern contexts, especially in India, due to the deep roots of Hindu mythology and the widespread influence of Indian culture and traditions.

name_in_real_life.story: Amit Dasharath, a teacher in Bali, Indonesia, shares that their name Dasharath meaning "Ten Chariots" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
